questions.q: What hatches out of a honeybee egg?
questions.fact: A larva! After about 3 days the egg hatches into a little white grub that nurse bees feed many times a day.

questions.q: What do worker bees put over a cell when the larva is ready to change into a pupa?
questions.fact: A wax cap! Sealed inside, the pupa grows legs, wings, and eyes before chewing its way out as a grown-up bee.

questions.q: About how many days does a worker bee take to grow from egg to adult?
questions.fact: About 21 days! That's 3 days as an egg, about 6 as a larva, and about 12 as a pupa.

questions.q: Which honeybee grows from egg to adult the fastest?
questions.fact: The queen! Fed lots of royal jelly, she's ready in about 16 days, while workers take about 21 and drones about 24.
